text:
sre-alex: Heads up — apiserver p95 jumped from ~40ms to ~600ms in eu-west1 at ~03:12 UTC, spike lasts ~8m. Noticed GPU attach queue length rising too.
eng-ops-bot: [alert] apiserver latency p95 > 500ms (eu-west1) — 03:12 UTC — correlating signals: conntrack_count=~65534, controller-manager leader flaps=3 in 5m.
infra-maya: on it, checking NAT instances and conntrack. ran `sudo conntrack -C` on nat-01-eu to confirm counts.
oncall-chris: any config changes rolled recently?
sre-alex: no deploys at that time. We did increase burst autoscale window for GPU pool last night, but shouldn't touch NAT.
infra-jen: looking at Cloud NAT metrics — simultaneous flows spiked, SNAT sessions nearing per-instance quota. probable 1-2k ephemeral port exhaustion patterns.
infra-maya: pulling `kubectl get endpoints -n kube-system` and `kubectl get pods -o wide` for apiserver + controllers. apiserver replicas healthy but many connection resets to NAT IP.
pm-jordan: if NAT is saturated, it explains heartbeat retries and leader election jitter — could cascade into controller-manager requeues and GPU provisioning delays (cost and SLA hit).
oncall-chris: mitigation options? reduce NAT connection churn, or add another NAT instance. Which is faster?
infra-jen: fastest: add one NAT instance behind the existing pool (manual scale). safer: enable ephemeral port reuse & conntrack tuning, but that requires rollout and might take longer.
sre-alex: can we temporarily route control-plane egress through regional bastion (bypass Cloud NAT) for apiserver heartbeats?
infra-maya: possible but needs firewall rules and small downtime window for NAT failover. I'll try scale + short-term conntrack flush on affected NATs.
eng-ops-bot: runbook: `actions/scale-nat` invoked by infra-maya at 03:17 UTC.
infra-maya: scaled NAT pool + flushed conntrack on nat-01-eu and nat-02-eu `sudo conntrack -F` — monitoring.
sre-alex: after flush, p95 down to ~80ms within 90s. GPU attach queue shrank from 420 -> 30 in 4m.
pm-jordan: good — but we need root cause and cost decision: adding permanent NAT capacity increases monthly egress gateway cost. tradeoff vs reconnect storms causing GPU retries (extra GPU hours).
infra-jen: collecting packet-level stats and port allocation histograms, will drop logs into the incident ticket. Suggest we add auto-scale for NAT or move control-plane egress to dedicated low-churn gateways for apiserver/controller-manager.
oncall-chris: temporary postmortem action: 1) enable NAT autoscale, 2) add alert for conntrack util >= 70%, 3) review kernel conntrack timeouts for control-plane pods.
sre-alex: agreed. followups: infra-jen to propose cost delta by EOD, pm-jordan to prioritize on roadmap if >$X/month and reduces GPU wasted hours.
infra-maya: saving logs and timings: attaching small snippet —
```
03:12:02 conntrack_count=65480
03:12:45 apiserver_p95=612ms
03:13:00 gpu_attach_queue=420
03:17:05 conntrack_flush
03:18:30 apiserver_p95=78ms
03:19:00 gpu_attach_queue=30
```

oncall-chris: thanks. creating incident ticket: INC-2026-4587 and assigning follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
pm-jordan: let's also add a small eval: run synthetic apiserver heartbeat through new NAT instance for 24h to see churn pattern before committing to permanent capacity increase.
sre-alex: good call. marking thread resolved for immediate mitigation, keeping monitoring open for 24h.
